clue.text: Comfortable seat Conservative surprisingly held: it's free

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so the following words come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken together as raw material

explanation.surface: A comfy armchair that a Tory was startled to find he could have for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'it's free' look like a separate remark, but its letters join 'held' as the material to rearrange after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a deeply padded leather sofa with buttoned back and rolled arms, a classic piece of upholstered furniture.

clue.text: Super money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, a rather old-fashioned British exclamation of approval
second meaning: funds invested or available for a business

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest a vast fortune, but they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word is dated British slang for splendid; as a noun it means the funds a business owns or raises.

clue.text: Emperor resigns over housing blunder

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
the phrase houses the wanted letters, holding them inside across the gap between its words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of emperor and the start of resigns

explanation.surface: An emperor abdicates because of some scandal he has been sheltering.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'empeROR REsigns' sit the letters RORRE; read upwards they spell ERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, and a blunder is a clumsy or careless mistake, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Untutored cast assembled

indicators.note: to cast something is to throw it or mould it afresh, so the word before is reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An amateur theatre company gathered for rehearsal, none of them trained actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the noun for a troupe of actors, which fits 'untutored' and 'assembled'; it is a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: When people turn out for an event they come together and gather, so the phrase in the past tense means gathered.

clue.text: Offensive letter you read, polite last of all

indicators.note: the last of every one of the listed words is wanted, the final letter of each in turn

parts.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone receives an insulting letter, though they read it politely right to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending of each of four words is wanted; 'polite' is a joke, being the very opposite of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rude is impolite and likely to cause hurt or insult, which is what offensive remarks or behaviour do.

clue.text: Argon, say, is great after mixing around nitrogen

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the chemical symbol that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: once the words have been mixed up, their letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: argon is fine once blended and wrapped round some nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface is the camouflage; nitrogen supplies only its symbol, slotted after the first letter of the shuffled pair of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is one of the noble gases that rarely react with other elements; 'say' marks it as an example of the class.

clue.text: Enjoy young setter from Hollywood, say?

parts.note: Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles, abbreviated LA; 'say' marks it as one example of a part of that city
a setter is a gundog breed, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Someone delights in a puppy of a gundog breed imported from Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is not the crossword compiler here but the dog breed, and the Hollywood puppy reads as an LA pup.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up something is an idiom for receiving it eagerly and with obvious pleasure, like a dog drinking.

clue.text: On level south of French border

indicators.note: in a down clue, being south of something means sitting below it, so these pieces come after

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for French
taken as written
a tier is one level of a stacked arrangement, like seating

explanation.surface: Standing on flat ground just below the boundary with France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French border' looks like a single geographic phrase; French is wordplay and border alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the line or region where one country meets another, which is the meaning of a border between states.

clue.text: Turn pale while squeezing it

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to grip it tightly, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: while and when both mean at the time that
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's knuckles go pale as they grip something hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiten is to become white or lose colour, as a face does in shock or fear.

clue.text: Character with edge in game

parts.note: an actor's part is the character they play
a ridge is a narrow raised edge or crest

explanation.surface: A player in some board game who is a bit of an edgy personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here is the culinary and shooting sense: wild birds hunted for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump bird shot in season for sport and eaten, so it counts as game.

clue.text: Fish rest like birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a freshwater fish with spiny fins
second meaning: to settle on a branch or bar, as birds do

explanation.surface: Fish taking a break the way birds do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a verb in a sentence about resting; it is a noun naming one meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a common spiny-finned river fish; the verb means to sit or alight on something raised, like a roosting bird.

clue.text: Christmas favourite, failure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bird roasted for the traditional festive dinner
second meaning: slang for a flop, especially a play or film

explanation.surface: A popular festive treat that turned out to be a let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The roast bird is the centrepiece of a traditional British holiday dinner, and in slang a show that flops is called one.

clue.text: How might one kill a creepy-crawly? Be quick!

definitions.text: How might one kill a creepy-crawly?
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: bring a foot down on the insect
second meaning: a hurry-up phrase, from pressing down on a car's accelerator

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal instruction to squash a bug underfoot; the second is the same phrase as idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order to hurry up, originally telling a driver to press the accelerator pedal down hard.

clue.text: Very many for example eaten by wild animal

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: a lion is a big wild cat
EG is the abbreviation of the Latin exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A wild beast devours prey, as happens to a great number of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a verb, as in 'their numbers are legion', the word is an adjective meaning numerous or countless.

clue.text: Stop cutting allowance in bank

indicators.note: a word cutting into another splits it apart and sits between its halves

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money allowed for a purpose
an engine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: A bank stopping someone's overdraft allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' points to money, matching 'allowance'; it is the slope of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the slope or incline of a surface, and a bank is a sloping stretch of ground beside a river or road.

clue.text: North American princess in ancient civilization

indicators.note: the royal piece is put inside the ancient land that follows

parts.note: Canaan was the ancient land of the Bible, roughly modern Israel and Lebanon
Di was the popular name for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A princess from the New World visiting the ruins of an old civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a person from Canada, the large country occupying the northern part of that continent.

clue.text: Man spared wrong sign in text

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of their proper order and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man escapes punishment after a mistaken message is sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' suggests a signal or omen in a story; here it is a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the written symbol &, standing for the word 'and' in printed or handwritten text.

clue.text: Old fossil is around, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go awry, so the preceding letters are disarranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old fogey is still hanging about, more's the pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal; it is plain letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a person with outdated views, likened to an extinct prehistoric creature.

clue.text: Weaken soil in land

indicators.note: the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: as a verb, to land a prize or contract is to win it
earth and soil are the ground plants grow in

explanation.surface: Soil that becomes depleted on a patch of farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' reads as a noun beside 'soil', but it is the verb, as in landing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearing thin, like patience or an excuse, is growing weaker and losing its force or effect.

clue.text: Breakfast nonsense?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grid-patterned batter cake eaten in the morning
second meaning: long-winded empty talk or writing

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words seem to sneer at someone's morning meal; they are two senses of one word, one a noun naming a food item.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a crisp batter cake eaten at the morning meal; it also means vague, padded talk, chiefly in British use.

clue.text: Ancient city where paintings etc shown in spring

indicators.note: works shown in a gallery are inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
paintings, sculptures and the like are art

explanation.surface: An old town where an art exhibition is staged each spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' suggests the season of an exhibition; it is a natural water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece, famous for its warrior culture and rivalry with Athens.

clue.text: Beaten, alas no winner, ultimately?

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the words after it are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the final letter of winner

explanation.surface: A sigh for the competitor who was beaten and ended up no winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: read as wordplay it builds the answer, read straight it describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that finishes out of the places, so it is beaten and never wins.

clue.text: Shoe: lose it, disaster!

parts.note: to flip is to lose your temper
a flop is a complete failure

explanation.surface: A shoe comes off, and someone shouts that it is a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flop is a light rubber sandal held on by a thong between the toes, a kind of open footwear.

clue.text: Scottish runner just out of the medals, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the answer is spelt differently from the phrase it matches

parts.note: finishing just behind gold, silver and bronze is coming in after third place

explanation.surface: A Scottish athlete narrowly misses a podium place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, which suits the medals; it is a river, since rivers run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forth is a major river in Scotland flowing into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh; a river is a crossword runner.

clue.text: Supporter runs behind leader in battle

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun naming one item, a pair of straps, so a singular definition fits

indicators.note: one piece comes behind the other, so it is placed after it in the answer
the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of battle
races are runs, as in competitive running events

explanation.surface: A fan running behind the commander as they go into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces are what Americans call suspenders: straps over the shoulders holding up trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces hold up a pair of trousers, so they act as a supporter in the literal sense of something that holds up.

clue.text: What fielder tries to do for contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: take the ball cleanly before it bounces in cricket or baseball
second meaning: to pick up an illness

explanation.surface: A player in the field aiming to win a new deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' suggests a player's deal; it is the verb meaning to come down with something, as in a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder aims to hold the struck ball to dismiss the batter, and to contract a disease is to pick it up.

clue.text: Some ruler, a Jaipur prince

indicators.note: only some of the following words is wanted, a part lying within them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of ruler, the word a and the start of Jaipur

explanation.surface: A sovereign from the Indian city of Jaipur.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaipur is a city in Rajasthan, India, which makes the hidden Indian title apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian king or prince, a title used for hereditary rulers of princely states.

clue.text: Ship concerned with nothing on return trip?

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: re means about or concerning
nil is nothing, a zero score

explanation.surface: A vessel that carries no cargo on the homeward voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger vessel that sails a regular route, so it is a kind of ship.

clue.text: A soldier, say, filling new crate easily

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so this piece is placed within the other
a new version of a word is a remade one, its letters set in fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a soldier ant is a kind of ant; 'say' marks soldier as one example

explanation.surface: A soldier packs a newly delivered box without any bother.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect, not a serviceman; a canter is a horse's relaxed, unhurried pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To win at a canter is an idiom for winning comfortably, from a horse not needing to gallop.

clue.text: Immediately at that place, further in the past

parts.note: there means in or at that place
and adds something further
then means at that earlier time

explanation.surface: A string of time and place phrases, as if pinning down when something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on the spot, at once, without any delay, which is what immediately means.
